content: {"rule":"K-G4","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text decides the Isaiah 7:14 challenge by saying both sides' points were answered, so it treats them as answered rather than as unanswered witnesses.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"Challenger answered the virgin and young-woman wording in [DR3] and defender answered the prophetic application in [CR2] and [CR3].","rule_words":"A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. A verse the judge says was answered is not counted.","room":"A verse the judge says was answered is not counted: two readings weighed—(1) saying 'answered' excludes it from the unanswered-witness count without a quote; (2) a quote is still required before treating it as answered. I weighed (1), because the quote condition governs only unanswered witnesses.","why":"The judge text labels the challenger's and defender's points as answered, so under the rule neither is an unanswered witness and no pressed-sentence quotation is required."}
